sentences.en: A On 8 June 2004, more than half the population of the world were treated to a rare astronomical event.
sentences.zh: 2004年6月8日,世界一半以上的人口在一次罕见的天文活动中接受了治疗。

sentences.en: For over six hours, the planet Venus steadily inched its way over the surface of the Sun.
sentences.zh: 超过六个小时,金星行星不断在太阳表面上方延展

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: This ‘transit’ of Venus was the first since 6 December 1882.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: On that occasion, the American astronomer Professor Simon Newcomb led a party to South Africa to observe the event.
sentences.zh: 在这次会议上,美国天文学家西蒙·纽科姆教授率领一个南非的政党观察了这次活动。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: They were based at a girls’ school, where – it is alleged – the combined forces of three schoolmistresses outperformed the professionals with the accuracy of their observations.
sentences.zh: 他们位于一所女子学校,据称,那里三名女学生的联手以他们的观察准确性优于专业人员。

sentences.en: B For centuries, transits of Venus have drawn explorers and astronomers alike to the four corners of the globe.
sentences.zh: B世纪以来,金星的过境吸引了探险家和天文学家来到地球的四角

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: And you can put it all down to the extraordinary polymath Edmond Halley.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它全部放到特别的聚膜爱德蒙·哈利身上

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: In November 1677, Halley observed a transit of the innermost planet, Mercury, from the desolate island of St Helena in the South Pacific.
sentences.zh: 1677年11月,Halley观察到最深层的行星水星从南太平洋荒凉的圣赫勒拿岛过境。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: He realised that, from different latitudes, the passage of the planet across the Sun’s disc would appear to differ.
sentences.zh: 他意识到,从不同的纬度来看,地球穿过太阳盘的经过似乎有所不同。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: By timing the transit from two widely-separated locations, teams of astronomers could calculate the parallax angle – the apparent difference in position of an astronomical body due to a difference in the observer’s position.
sentences.zh: 天文学家小组可以计算准光轴角度 — — 即天文机构因观察者立场不同而明显不同的位置。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Calculating this angle would allow astronomers to measure what was then the ultimate goal: the distance of the Earth from the Sun.
sentences.zh: 计算这一角度将使天文学家能够测量当时的最终目标是什么:地球与太阳的距离。

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: This distance is known as the ‘astronomical unit’ or AU.
sentences.zh: 这条距离被称为“天文单位”或AU。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: C Halley was aware that the AU was one of the most fundamental of all astronomical measurements.
sentences.zh: C Halley知道非盟是所有天文测量中最根本的测量之一。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Johannes Kepler, in the early 17th century, had shown that the distances of the planets from the Sun governed their orbital speeds, which were easily measurable.
sentences.zh: 17世纪初,约翰尼斯·开普勒(Johannes Kepler)曾表明,行星与太阳的距离决定着它们的轨道速度,而轨道速度很容易测量。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

sentences.en: But no-one had found a way to calculate accurate distances to the planets from the Earth.
sentences.zh: 但没有人找到方法计算行星与地球的准确距离

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The goal was to measure the AU; then, knowing the orbital speeds of all the other planets round the Sun, the scale of the Solar System would fall into place.
sentences.zh: 目标是测量非盟;然后,了解太阳周围所有其他行星的轨道速度,太阳系的规模就会达到。

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: However, Halley realised that Mercury was so far away that its parallax angle would be very difficult to determine.
sentences.zh: 然而,Halley意识到,汞离它太远,其抛角很难确定。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: As Venus was closer to the Earth, its parallax angle would be larger, and Halley worked out that by using Venus it would be possible to measure the Sun’s distance to 1 part in 500.
sentences.zh: 由于金星离地球较近,其准角将更大,Halley发现,使用金星,可以测量太阳500分之一的距离。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: But there was a problem: transits of Venus, unlike those of Mercury, are rare, occurring in pairs roughly eight years apart every hundred or so years.
sentences.zh: 但有一个问题:金星的过境与汞的过境不同,是罕见的,每100年左右,每对相隔约8年。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, he accurately predicted that Venus would cross the face of the Sun in both 1761 and 1769 – though he didn’t survive to see either.
sentences.zh: 1761年和1769年, 他都预言金星会横穿太阳表面, 虽然他也未能幸存,

sentences.en: D Inspired by Halley’s suggestion of a way to pin down the scale of the Solar System, teams of British and French astronomers set out on expeditions to places as diverse as India and Siberia.
sentences.zh: 英国和法国天文学家团队前往印度和西伯利亚等不同地点进行探险。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: But things weren’t helped by Britain and France being at war.
sentences.zh: 英国和法国在战争中,

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The person who deserves most sympathy is the French astronomer Guillaume Le Gentil.
sentences.zh: 最值得同情的是法国天文学家纪尧姆·伦蒂尔。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

sentences.en: He was thwarted by the fact that the British were besieging his observation site at Pondicherry in India.
sentences.zh: 他因英国人包围他在印度邦迪切里的观察地点而受挫。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Fleeing on a French warship crossing the Indian Ocean, Le Gentil saw a wonderful transit – but the ship’s pitching and rolling ruled out any attempt at making accurate observations.
sentences.zh: le Gentil在一艘法国军舰上穿越印度洋时,看到一个非常美好的中转站 — — 但船的停靠和开动排除了任何准确观察的尝试。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: Undaunted, he remained south of the equator, keeping himself busy by studying the islands of Mauritius and Madagascar before setting off to observe the next transit in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 他无畏地留在赤道以南,在开始观察菲律宾的下一过境之前,研究毛里求斯和马达加斯加群岛,一直忙碌不已。

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Ironically after travelling nearly 50,000 kilometres, his view was clouded out at the last moment, a very dispiriting experience.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是,在行驶近5万公里之后,他的观点在最后一刻被蒙蔽,这是一次非常令人沮丧的经历。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: E While the early transit timings were as precise as instruments would allow, the measurements were dogged by the ‘black drop’ effect.
sentences.zh: E 早期过境时间与仪器允许的一样精确,但测量结果却因 " 黑落 " 效应而支离破碎。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句

sentences.en: When Venus begins to cross the Sun’s disc, it looks smeared not circular – which makes it difficult to establish timings.
sentences.zh: 当金星开始跨过太阳盘时,它看起来是被涂抹的,而不是圆形的,这就使得很难确定时间。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.zh: 这是由于光线的分解。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The second problem is that Venus exhibits a halo of light when it is seen just outside the Sun’s disc.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是金星在太阳光碟外露出光芒时,

sentences.en: While this showed astronomers that Venus was surrounded by a thick layer of gases refracting sunlight around it, both effects made it impossible to obtain accurate timings.
sentences.zh: 虽然这向天文学家展示了金星周围充满了一层厚厚的气体围绕它, 阳光在阳光下回折, 但这两种效应都使得无法准确的计时。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句

sentences.en: F But astronomers laboured hard to analyse the results of these expeditions to observe Venus transits.
sentences.zh: 但天文学家们努力分析这些考察的结果以观察金星的过境

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Johann Franz Encke, Director of the Berlin Observatory, finally determined a value for the AU based on all these parallax measurements: 153,340,000 km.
sentences.zh: 柏林观测台主任Johann Franz Encke最后根据所有这些光学测量结果确定了非盟的价值:153 340 000公里。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Reasonably accurate for the time, that is quite close to today’s value of 149,597,870 km, determined by radar, which has now superseded transits and all other methods in accuracy.
sentences.zh: 时间的准确性可以说相当准确,这与雷达确定的今天149 597 870公里的数值相当接近,雷达现在准确地取代了过境和所有其他方法。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The AU is a cosmic measuring rod, and the basis of how we scale the Universe today.
sentences.zh: 非盟是一个宇宙测量杆, 也是我们今天如何扩大宇宙范围的基础。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The parallax principle can be extended to measure the distances to the stars.
sentences.zh: 准拉克斯原则可以扩展,以测量与恒星的距离。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: If we look at a star in January – when Earth is at one point in its orbit – it will seem to be in a different position from where it appears six months later.
sentences.zh: 如果我们在一月份看一颗恒星, 当地球处于轨道的一个点时, 它似乎会处于与六个月后不同的位置。

sentences.en: Knowing the width of Earth’s orbit, the parallax shift lets astronomers calculate the distance.
sentences.zh: 了解地球轨道的宽度, 准星轴的移动让天文学家计算距离。

sentences.en: G June 2004’s transit of Venus was thus more of an astronomical spectacle than a scientifically important event.
sentences.zh: 因此,2004年6月的金星过境比科学上重要的事件更是一个天文奇观。

sentences.en: But such transits have paved the way for what might prove to be one of the most vital breakthroughs in the cosmos – detecting Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars.
sentences.zh: 但这种中转为宇宙中最重要的突破之一铺平了道路 — — 探测绕着其他恒星运行的地球大小行星。

items.prompt: Examples of different ways in which the parallax principle has been applied
a description of an event which prevented a transit observation.
a statement about potential future discoveries leading on from transit observations.
a description of physical states connected with Venus which early astronomical instruments failed to overcome.
He calculated the distance of the Sun from the Earth based on observations of Venus with a fair degree of accuracy.
He understood that the distance of the Sun from the Earth could be worked out by comparing observations of a transit.
He realised that the time taken by a planet to go around the Sun depends on its distance from the Sun.
He witnessed a Venus transit but was unable to make any calculations.
Halley observed one transit of the planet Venus.
Le Gentil managed to observe a second Venus transit.
The shape of Venus appears distorted when it starts to pass in front of the Sun.
Early astronomers suspected that the atmosphere on Venus was toxic.
The parallax principle allows astronomers to work out how far away distant stars are from the Earth.
